name: Calculator
highLevelGoals: The user aims to accurately and efficiently perform fundamental arithmetic calculations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) using the smartphone calculator app.
The user desires an intuitive and straightforward interface that allows for effortless input of numbers and selection of operations, minimizing cognitive load and errors.
The user expects calculation results to be displayed prominently and updated instantly, ensuring quick verification and confidence in the app's accuracy.
The user requires the calculator app to consistently provide correct results for all basic operations, including proper handling of edge cases like division by zero.
lowLevelGoals: The user can press a numeric button (0-9) to display the corresponding digit on the calculator screen.
The user can press an operation button (+, -, *, /) to select the desired arithmetic function.
The user can press the equals button (=) to trigger the calculation and display the result.
The user can press the 'C' or 'AC' button to clear the current input or reset the calculator.
The user can press the decimal point button (.) to enter decimal numbers.
The user can input multiple digits consecutively to form a multi-digit number on the calculator display.
The user can tap an operation button (+, -, *, /) to register the desired arithmetic function for the ongoing calculation.
The user sees a visual change (e.g., button highlight) when a button is pressed, confirming input.
The user can see the numbers and operations they are currently entering on the calculator's display area.
The user can clearly see the final calculated result displayed in a prominent area of the calculator screen.
The user sees the result appear on the display immediately after pressing the equals button.
The user sees a clear error message (e.g., 'Error', 'Cannot divide by zero') when attempting to divide by zero.
The user receives the mathematically correct sum when performing addition.
The user receives the mathematically correct difference when performing subtraction.
The user receives the mathematically correct product when performing multiplication.
The user receives the mathematically correct quotient when performing division.
